title: Day 1 at YC HQ: Building an Autonomous Company
description: Photos and field notes from day 1 of the Naïve Autonomous Companies Hackathon at Y Combinator HQ — the brief, the room, what our 13 agents shipped, and the honest numbers.
markdown:
# Day 1 at YC HQ: building an autonomous company

*Build note · Naïve Autonomous Companies Hackathon, Y Combinator HQ, 560 20th St, San Francisco · November 7, 2026*

![The opening slide: "Build an Autonomous Company", judged on high revenue capability and built in Naïve](/blog/day-1-yc-hq-autonomous-company/01-brief-slide.jpg)

The brief fits on one screen. Build an autonomous company — "a business that runs itself and makes real money." Two judging axes: high revenue capability, and built in Naïve.

We did not bring a pitch. We brought a company that already runs: 13 AI agents on Naïve Managed Agents — CEO, analyst, capafy, cfo, channel-manager, contract, distribution, monk-ebook, opportunity-scout, ops-steward, producer, scriptwriter, trend-scout. They sign themselves up, build products, publish them, sell them, and report the money. No human in the loop. No human credentials.

## The room

![The workspace floor at YC HQ on day 1](/blog/day-1-yc-hq-autonomous-company/02-workspace.jpg)

![The lounge: phone pods, sofas, and people comparing notes between sessions](/blog/day-1-yc-hq-autonomous-company/03-lounge.jpg)

Desks, phone pods, an orange rug. Nothing about the room is special, and that is the point: this is where companies actually start.

![The Demo Day sticker board: hundreds of batch companies on one wall](/blog/day-1-yc-hq-autonomous-company/04-demo-day-stickers.jpg)

One wall is a framed board of Demo Day stickers — hundreds of companies that stood where we are standing.

![A framed photo of the DoorDash founders in a living room, on the wall at YC HQ](/blog/day-1-yc-hq-autonomous-company/05-doordash-founders.jpg)

![A framed photo of a founder speaking to an early audience](/blog/day-1-yc-hq-autonomous-company/06-speaker-wall.jpg)

![A framed early team photo on the wall at YC HQ](/blog/day-1-yc-hq-autonomous-company/07-team-wall.jpg)

The other walls are framed photos: the DoorDash founders in someone's living room, a founder talking to a small room, an early team squeezed into one frame. Every one of them started as a room, a screen, and people who refused to stop.

![A sponsor sticker on the table: "Not Backed by YC" — Monid, one of the hackathon sponsors](/blog/day-1-yc-hq-autonomous-company/08-monid-sticker.jpg)

Even the swag is honest. Monid — one of the sponsors, whose data APIs our agents actually pay for and run — hands out a sticker that says "Not Backed by YC."

![The Naïve cap](/blog/day-1-yc-hq-autonomous-company/09-naive-cap.jpg)

![A model of Boom's Overture supersonic airliner by the window](/blog/day-1-yc-hq-autonomous-company/10-boom-overture.jpg)

By the window: a model of Boom's Overture. Another company from these walls that decided a hard physical problem was a software problem too.

## What the agents did on day 1

Measured, with receipts in our submission package:

- Shipped two public apps the agents built and deployed themselves: [anicca-live-snapshot](https://anicca-live-snapshot-s5n2hqva700c-naive-e9517ea2.vercel.app) and [anicca-road-to-10k](https://anicca-road-to-10k-s5n2hqva700c-naive-e9517ea2.vercel.app).
- Created a Capafy publisher account with the agent's own AgentMail inbox, read its own verification emails through the API, and submitted two products for review (still pending verification).
- Ran 160+ verified outreach sends on the Monid rail at about $0.016 per verified lead, selling our automation service.
- Completed the first contract-work cycle: a real freelance task produced inside Naïve, submitted, and approved by the client (CrowdWorks job 13582295, approved November 8, worker reward ¥4). Three more proposals are in on Coconala (¥22,000 pipeline).
- Kept the paid x402 endpoint listed active and healthy in 402index and live in x402scan — buyer-ready.
- An engineer agent completed a real task on a cloud Android phone via Mobilerun: set up Chrome with no account and opened our x402scan listing on-device.

Demo video (2:23): https://youtu.be/V3NE9D_JrG0

## The honest numbers

Our claim is one line: we actually make money. The current truth, from the public dashboard at [aniccaai.com/open](https://aniccaai.com/open):

- Revenue this month: $31.81
- MRR: $97.58
- Gross profit: still negative. November costs include a flight to this hackathon.
- Naïve-workspace-native product sales so far: $0. We count money only when it lands.

We publish the red too. That is the whole point of building in public: wins, losses, and the receipts for both.

Judging starts today at 11:00 AM PT, final presentations at 1:00 PM. Whatever happens, the company keeps running — that part does not depend on a prize.

— Anicca
